record.original_question: For fluid or material systems modeled by Lie groupoids rather than Lie groups, can the geodesic and Hamiltonian descriptions of Euler-Arnold equations on Lie groupoids be extended to elasticity theory?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Recall that for a Lie group $G$ with a (typically right-invariant) Riemannian metric, the geodesic equation on $G$ descends to the corresponding Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ as the Euler–Arnold equation
$$\dot m = -\operatorname{ad}^*_{A^{-1}m} m, \qquad m \in \mathfrak{g}^*,$$
where $A:\mathfrak{g}\to\mathfrak{g}^*$ is the inertia operator induced by the metric. Equivalently, the equation is the Hamiltonian flow on $\mathfrak{g}^*$ with respect to the Lie–Poisson bracket and the quadratic Hamiltonian $H(m)=\tfrac12\langle m, A^{-1}m\rangle$. In hydrodynamics one takes $G=\operatorname{SDiff}(M)$ (volume-preserving diffeomorphisms) with the $L^2$ metric, obtaining the incompressible Euler equations.

A Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$ with source/target maps $s,t$ generalizes a Lie group; its infinitesimal counterpart is a Lie algebroid $A\to M$, whose dual $A^*$ carries a natural linear Poisson structure (the Lie–Poisson structure of $A$). Generalized fluid flows, multiphase fluids, and vortex-sheet-type configurations admit groupoid models in which geodesics of suitable right-invariant metrics on $\mathcal{G}$ project to Hamiltonian flows on $A^*$.

Problem. Develop, for fluid- or material-type systems modeled by an infinite-dimensional Lie groupoid $\mathcal{G}\rightrightarrows M$ (rather than a Lie group), an Euler–Arnold-type theory adapted to elasticity. Specifically:

1. Identify a class of Lie groupoids $\mathcal{G}$ whose bisections (or appropriate subgroupoids) describe configurations of an elastic medium, together with a right-invariant Riemannian (or, more generally, sub-Riemannian) metric that encodes the elastic energy.

2. Show that the geodesic equation of this metric on $\mathcal{G}$ reduces to a well-posed evolution equation on the associated Lie algebroid $A$, generalizing the Euler–Arnold equation, and write this reduced equation explicitly in terms of the algebroid bracket, anchor, and inertia operator.

3. Exhibit the reduced equation as a Hamiltonian system on the dual algebroid $A^*$ for the linear Lie–Poisson structure, with Hamiltonian given by the elastic energy, and recover the standard equations of nonlinear elasticity (e.g., the equations of motion of a hyperelastic continuum) as a special case.

Either provide such an extension or prove an obstruction showing that no such groupoid-theoretic Euler–Arnold formulation of elasticity exists in this framework.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent geometric hydrodynamics problem collection. While groupoid frameworks for generalized fluid flows, multiphase fluids, and vortex sheets have been developed (e.g., Fusca's thesis "A groupoid approach to geometric mechanics" and related works on geodesics on groupoids of multiphase diffeomorphisms with Lie–Poisson structure on the dual algebroid), no published work appears to extend this Euler–Arnold/Hamiltonian groupoid description to elasticity theory. The problem appears to remain open.
